outcome: Sworn's OpenAI-compatible driver admits Google and xAI as first-class providers by handling their wire dialects at named extension points: Google's per-message opaque thought signatures are retained and replayed byte-exact on every subsequent turn or the dispatch is refused, and xAI's vendor usage decorations are admitted without weakening strict decoding anywhere else, so gemini-3.7-flash and grok-4.6 certify and can carry roles.

exclude: relaxing strict decoding into tolerance of unknown fields anywhere except the named extension points
parsing, interpreting or persisting the content of any opaque vendor field
changes to token budgeting, streaming, or the continuation step and field limits

acceptance.text: A chat-completions assistant message carrying a vendor extension container (Google extra_content with a thought signature) decodes successfully, the container is retained as opaque continuation state, and the next request in the same invocation replays it byte-exact in the position the provider requires. A fixture from a recorded gemini-3.7-flash exchange proves decode, retention and byte-exact replay.

Replay is mandatory, not best-effort: if retained vendor continuation state cannot be replayed (evicted, over budget, or structurally unplaceable), the dispatch fails closed with a labelled error naming the mechanism, because the provider silently degrades rather than erroring when the signature is absent - the recorded two-turn probe in which the model contradicts its own prior turn without the signature is checked into the fixture set as the reason.

Usage blocks carrying vendor decorations (xAI's cost, source-count and context-detail fields, from a recorded grok-4.6 exchange) decode successfully on both the chat-completions and responses surfaces, and the token accounting Sworn reads is taken only from the standard fields.

Strictness is preserved everywhere else: an unknown field outside the named extension points still fails decoding with the same error it fails with today, and a test proves the extension points are an explicit allowlist rather than a global tolerance.

Opaque vendor state never crosses the trust boundary: nothing from an extension container appears in a submission, a receipt, a candidate, or the journal beyond the continuation ledger's existing opaque retention, and a test asserts it.

Driver certification passes for a Google chat-completions adapter with gemini-3.7-flash and an xAI responses adapter with grok-4.6 when replayed against the recorded certification fixtures, and the certification failure codes these providers produce today (certification_response_contract_failed, certification_usage_failed) are covered by regression fixtures so they cannot silently return.

constraints: Opaque means opaque: vendor extension bytes are retained and replayed, never parsed for meaning, never logged in full, and never persisted outside the continuation ledger.

Fail closed over degrade silently: the recorded probe shows the provider answers confidently with a broken reasoning chain when the signature is missing, so absence of replayable state is a refusal, never a retry without it.
The extension points are named per provider and per structural position; DisallowUnknownFields-style strictness remains the default at every other decode site.
The e2e check is declared, not executed by a role (ADR 0010).
Check evidence belongs in the submission's checks field, never in files added to the repository; the candidate diff carries only product, test and fixture changes.
